summaries.demographer: Sandi Chapman is a 26-year-old white woman born and living in Modesto, California, with an eighth-grade education and no GED as of the interview (Q85-Q90). She has never been married, has no children, and rents a two-bedroom apartment with one non-romantic roommate, Marisol Vega (Q11, Q51, Q84). Her household is a two-adult roommate household that splits rent and utilities, with Sandi earning service-sector wages and tips as a waitress (Q55, Q65, Q72). Her life course reflects working-class Central Valley roots, early school exit, and strong ongoing ties to parents, sibling, grandmother, coworkers, and local arts networks (Q01, Q05, Q07).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Sandi's choices show strong present constraints but clear future-oriented aspirations: she wants promotion, classes, GED completion, savings, and eventually a cafe-gallery, while coping with volatile tips and emergency expenses (Q18, Q61-Q63, Q108). She is liquidity constrained, with about $600 in savings and roughly $1,200 in credit card debt, so shocks such as car repairs alter work, food, and leisure behavior (Q61, Q63, Q81-Q82). Her labor supply responds to immediate financial pressure through extra shifts, reduced discretionary spending, and cooking at home (Q60, Q81). Identity and peer networks also shape her decisions, as art, hospitality, and friends motivate her career plans and social consumption (Q07, Q17, Q48, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Sandi is a left-leaning, weak-to-moderate Democrat who votes in presidential elections and some state/local contests, usually by mail, but admits inconsistent participation in smaller elections (Q23, Q95-Q96). Her political concerns are material and local: rent, wages, health care, paid sick time, public transit, arts funding, and small-business viability (Q24-Q25). She supports racial justice, Black Lives Matter concerns, police accountability, LGBTQ rights, reproductive rights, and humane immigration policy (Q24, Q26-Q29). Her institutional trust is pragmatic rather than ideological; she trusts official health sources more than social media and wants politics to solve concrete problems for working people (Q24, Q42).
summaries.psychologist: Sandi presents as socially expressive, humorous, improvisational, and relationally oriented, with a self-concept built around hospitality, creativity, and making people feel seen (Q01, Q65, Q109). She also describes anxiety around money, schedules, and falling behind, though she has no formal diagnosis and uses movement, lists, friends, family, and creative events to regulate stress (Q43-Q45, Q50). Her early school exit remains a source of embarrassment and motivation, but she reframes it through competence gained in work and future plans for education (Q02-Q04, Q90, Q108). She is high in openness and social engagement, moderately disorganized, and motivated by connection, usefulness, and creative community-building (Q07, Q17, Q48, Q109).
